content.page_title: Cardiac rhythm management for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
content.section_header: 6 Cardiac rhythm management for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
content.summary: Provides recommendations on use of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICD) and cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Notes that a high proportion of deaths in HF are sudden and often due to electrical disturbances (ventricular arrhythmias, bradycardia, asystole) or acute vascular events. ICDs are effective at correcting potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmias and, for transvenous systems, can prevent bradycardia. Treatments that delay progression of cardiovascular disease reduce the annual rate of sudden death but do not treat arrhythmic events when they occur. Some antiarrhythmic drugs may reduce tachyarrhythmias and sudden death but do not reduce overall mortality and may increase it.
content.recommendation_notes: Figure shows management options with Class I and IIa recommendations; see specific tables for Class IIb recommendations. The section points to further detail in tables and figures.
